title: Adding by counting on a number line
examples: How do I add on a number line?
Which number should I start from?

explain.say: Imagine a frog sitting on a path of numbers. It is on 6, and it wants to make 5 hops. Where will it land? Look at the number line on the board, and let us hop together. It lands on 11!

draw.text: Adding by counting on a number line

explain.say: First, find the start. Put your finger on 6. That is where the frog sits. We do not count the 6 again, because the frog is already there. Can you find 6 on the line?
Now hop forward, one jump at a time: 7, 8. See the 2 hops? 6 and 2 make 8. Each hop adds 1. That is called counting on. Where will 3 more hops take us?
9, 10, 11. That is 5 hops in all, landing on 11! So 6 plus 5 equals 11. Adding means moving forward, to the right, on the number line. Which way would taking away go?
Great hopping! A clever trick: start with the bigger number. For 3 plus 9, start at 9 and hop just 3: 10, 11, 12. Much faster than 9 hops! Wow: a ruler is a number line too.

faq.a: Counting on means starting at one number and counting forward. For 6 plus 5, you start at 6 and count 7, 8, 9, 10, 11.

faq.q: How do I add on a number line?
faq.a: Put your finger on the first number, then make one hop to the right for each number you add. Where you land is the answer.
asks: How do I use a number line to add?

faq.q: Why don't I count the starting number?
faq.a: Because you are already standing there. The hops are the numbers you add, so the first hop goes to the next number.
asks: Do I count the number I start on?

faq.q: Which number should I start from?
faq.a: Start from the bigger number, then hop the smaller one. 3 plus 9 and 9 plus 3 give the same answer, but 3 hops are quicker than 9.
asks: Does it matter which number I start with?

faq.q: Which way do I go to take away?
faq.a: To take away, hop backwards, to the left. 11 take away 5 starts at 11 and hops back to 6.
asks: How do I subtract on a number line?

facts: Adding in either order gives the same answer: 3 + 9 = 9 + 3 = 12.

quiz.say: Start at 8 and make 4 hops forward. Where do you land?
quiz.show: Start at 8 and make 4 hops forward. Where do you land?

wrong.0: 11 counts the starting 8 as a hop.
wrong.1: 4 is the number of hops, not where you land.

quiz.say: What is the quickest way to work out 2 plus 9 on a number line?
quiz.show: What is the quickest way to work out 2 + 9 on a number line?
quiz.why: Starting at the bigger number, 9, and hopping 2 reaches 11 fastest.

wrong.1: Starting at 2 and hopping 2 only gives 4.
wrong.2: Starting at 0 and hopping 2 gives just 2.
